Mixing different types of alcohol (like beer, wine, and spirits) does not inherently cause worse hangovers or extra intoxication—the total amount of alcohol consumed and how fast you drink it matter most . However, mixing alcohol with other substances like medications, caffeine, or drugs can be dangerous.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF14cHFVDPxLTZg6Q1L4-5D6Cwve1Di4VUkeufv5bwmwuttx1YSQNi3Nwca59kq7lrsKSIgJDLartC60kXhM4YQmH5XsvjZYhdYpMpWjIkfulAPJ6O4WW9vhvwPrcWauLUsiNDHkgTTcvU8bUlOTL4B1tcVWtgLQZfI_lkJIy0CA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjAEBxCJF12ri3ZGyw-0mQagYF00C-LRz3kdOhizomnWZOzTbT5khAt2KIwum60g-yL054mmpkJuKdGWyDDj0A_hLDUuF6aS1zXUZa7upjSGFeIsYIJR0DVr1eZ-BFVjRhvkI2YB1EHuML1GmXIp71peId2ETHPOL2lqwArkXK40hudjXFTSuecmXKrsIlw)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEStAEBxCJF15vUW6HMv87YKzZVSA-NkkSc8W1MgrSuOBS1NhzGB0ZZpsjtYXjZXw4opXbdWne2RViDVhKGoLwh2CRcjMzMxPFSRKuWlthVjE_2R2TD_RgC8EzWUJMuFTAEUlvHNK9SdOr32EMjFibxYhiXiabKU4fUUW7E72GGKnkrrxNh9sw-DgUyhhSPVPkdxyuHbS2cm3zWUosm9KBxujpfa_R2X9E8drkiGsH-dW6kYCUHRdo)

### Why Mixing Drinks Can Still Feel Bad

- **Total volume and pacing:** Switching drinks makes it harder to track how much alcohol you have had. Starting with lower-alcohol drinks can impair judgment and lead you to drink stronger alcohol too quickly.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESqQEBxCJF15aN1c83dfNGl4_Tl-Pi9jFrIEzdQC7voCkvwIp_QMyY1ZEDStW7v2bR14rixC4IyYHEvqeFIHHnMiXpgWDlujsFjsZEvQXNcldvtwT0pYaNicQ0Gxo5niwOK8OXjaaBOFambylWQfjX54_7plnYiOaa-FygjqAz9EQbPPm4_bHs_czqx8zmC5BxO6V_zF3-jgVRZqyePKGAG2BlS5OOhwuYdEBv)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXiDvbyMuhDb1AGybRpppVfG6wiGY-utGGEJUDUMHrJAUiaSrherQSvSywDPzBlrt28dP-4Wx15rxg9CE7hhW16b9cRoZ-I53vtwEAGSkIjqV6tKKyUW5fQq2zUucsqTal8tjukJswJg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF14cHFVDPxLTZg6Q1L4-5D6Cwve1Di4VUkeufv5bwmwuttx1YSQNi3Nwca59kq7lrsKSIgJDLartC60kXhM4YQmH5XsvjZYhdYpMpWjIkfulAPJ6O4WW9vhvwPrcWauLUsiNDHkgTTcvU8bUlOTL4B1tcVWtgLQZfI_lkJIy0CA)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF14uJ7DKXotk6C07g3gMsfYEenq8Oz_mFkJjth9q3syXehX-JDeEkPszgIwPkqXjKc6Ckx_ncxwkZhbt0S7l7hrD4ULYa8GIbANG8i1BNYOqhZnjgExNIhEP7tUK1dh3l2_66aSYkA2lvIlw6BUsQL1N2v9iCc878M5gKoSBcD1g)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESsAEBxCJF105Wbc8jKFvHSeO_Xrlibh_DWgf8jCNu_wOILWy-6RFbeWsYp1T8msez2p2LrDWeReBqddlw1MkKcqTpD_xwVWI-QiE1gu39yAvi98fNwC8dQykOcX2S2eb1uYDAXzpA0Bad5bybfuRuhl1HfB-yPTxxrxwHoWsfhu5YpuzvTT27oPRzJZiCouu8dANvgcJrxdb4zhZ-Uc9VZ0T0pNqcyyP1mLPchkDbV4WjAw)
- **Congeners:** Darker drinks (like bourbon, whiskey, and red wine) contain more fermentation byproducts called congeners. High congener intake—not mixing itself—can worsen hangover symptoms and irritate the stomach.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXX3duoSmxKQyfsRBSjtrdyuCw5yteHYYQjCt7oQ5Qc8FFp0E6Np-CYkiLYuoC-_m-5Snt78j6Q8xRPk5MgEGXaVbrLg6Wb98pi4eBz1nndHd3-V0yaNQvlJbufhuDmh84bilgPSzNemobo7CCwEI8)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF14cHFVDPxLTZg6Q1L4-5D6Cwve1Di4VUkeufv5bwmwuttx1YSQNi3Nwca59kq7lrsKSIgJDLartC60kXhM4YQmH5XsvjZYhdYpMpWjIkfulAPJ6O4WW9vhvwPrcWauLUsiNDHkgTTcvU8bUlOTL4B1tcVWtgLQZfI_lkJIy0CA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlwEBxCJF1xhRguq7HE9j2NEzt87vJPP-V4J2BVK6vTyuu9yey5Ntx_g6NLT5EG3L7BWPYsPTF7g78OboDmXykv_PndTLCaIDA2raPj7BnMZKm2jE11enAMw60rFnTL7ENht-TIioj1cAXTE-_Jp7yOt-o5dyKt1j_J4o3uyRxOaf1v3vwuHrBX_hT_DByZspwWy_MWAMzieH)
- **Mixers and carbonation:** Sugary mixers can add extra calories and slow or alter how you feel, while carbonation can speed up alcohol absorption.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESqQEBxCJF15aN1c83dfNGl4_Tl-Pi9jFrIEzdQC7voCkvwIp_QMyY1ZEDStW7v2bR14rixC4IyYHEvqeFIHHnMiXpgWDlujsFjsZEvQXNcldvtwT0pYaNicQ0Gxo5niwOK8OXjaaBOFambylWQfjX54_7plnYiOaa-FygjqAz9EQbPPm4_bHs_czqx8zmC5BxO6V_zF3-jgVRZqyePKGAG2BlS5OOhwuYdEBv)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlwEBxCJF1xhRguq7HE9j2NEzt87vJPP-V4J2BVK6vTyuu9yey5Ntx_g6NLT5EG3L7BWPYsPTF7g78OboDmXykv_PndTLCaIDA2raPj7BnMZKm2jE11enAMw60rFnTL7ENht-TIioj1cAXTE-_Jp7yOt-o5dyKt1j_J4o3uyRxOaf1v3vwuHrBX_hT_DByZspwWy_MWAMzieH)

As a [BBC Future](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF14cHFVDPxLTZg6Q1L4-5D6Cwve1Di4VUkeufv5bwmwuttx1YSQNi3Nwca59kq7lrsKSIgJDLartC60kXhM4YQmH5XsvjZYhdYpMpWjIkfulAPJ6O4WW9vhvwPrcWauLUsiNDHkgTTcvU8bUlOTL4B1tcVWtgLQZfI_lkJIy0CA) review explains, hangovers are driven by dehydration, alcohol's toxic effects, immune and hormone changes, total ethanol intake, and congeners rather than the act of combining different types of alcohol.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF14cHFVDPxLTZg6Q1L4-5D6Cwve1Di4VUkeufv5bwmwuttx1YSQNi3Nwca59kq7lrsKSIgJDLartC60kXhM4YQmH5XsvjZYhdYpMpWjIkfulAPJ6O4WW9vhvwPrcWauLUsiNDHkgTTcvU8bUlOTL4B1tcVWtgLQZfI_lkJIy0CA)

### When Mixing Is Truly Risky

- **Medications or other drugs:** Combining alcohol with prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, or other sedatives can cause severe side effects, liver strain, slowed breathing, or overdose.
- **Energy drinks or stimulants:** Caffeine can mask how intoxicated you feel, making it easier to drink too much and risk alcohol poisoning.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEStAEBxCJF15vUW6HMv87YKzZVSA-NkkSc8W1MgrSuOBS1NhzGB0ZZpsjtYXjZXw4opXbdWne2RViDVhKGoLwh2CRcjMzMxPFSRKuWlthVjE_2R2TD_RgC8EzWUJMuFTAEUlvHNK9SdOr32EMjFibxYhiXiabKU4fUUW7E72GGKnkrrxNh9sw-DgUyhhSPVPkdxyuHbS2cm3zWUosm9KBxujpfa_R2X9E8drkiGsH-dW6kYCUHRdo)
